invariants_created: Host header is mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request
Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding is required when a request or response has a body
POST, PUT, and PATCH requests should include a body with a Content-Type header
HEAD response must not include a message body
After receiving 401 Unauthorized, client must retry the request with an Authorization header
After receiving a 3xx redirect response, client should follow the Location header to the new URI
Connection: close header signals the connection will be closed after the response is sent
Persistent connections (keep-alive) allow multiple request-response cycles on a single TCP connection
OPTIONS * targets the server as a whole rather than a specific resource path
Request line must come first, followed by headers, then an empty line (CRLF CRLF), then optional body
State transition: INIT → TCP connect → CONNECTED → send request → RESPONSE_PENDING → receive response → IDLE (or AUTH_REQUIRED on 401, or follow redirect on 3xx, or CLOSED on Connection: close)
After 301/302 redirect, the client issues a new GET request to the Location URI before proceeding with other operations
Safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) should not modify server state; idempotent methods (GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE) produce same result on repeated calls
HTTP REQUEST.Host: Mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request; identifies the target virtual host
HTTP REQUEST.Content-Length: Required when request body is present; must accurately reflect byte length of body
HTTP REQUEST.Transfer-Encoding: Alternative to Content-Length when body is present; 'chunked' allows streaming without known length
HTTP REQUEST.Content-Type: Should be included for POST, PUT, and PATCH requests that have a body (e.g., application/json)
HTTP REQUEST.Authorization: Must be included when retrying after a 401 Unauthorized response; carries credentials for protected resources
HTTP REQUEST.Method: Must be one of: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, CONNECT, TRACE; determines semantics (safe, idempotent, body requirements)
HTTP REQUEST.Request-URI: Target resource path; '*' for server-level OPTIONS request
HTTP REQUEST.Connection: 'keep-alive' (default) for persistent connections; 'close' to terminate connection after response
HTTP RESPONSE.Status-Code: 3-digit code: 2xx=success, 3xx=redirection, 4xx=client error, 5xx=server error; determines client behavior (retry auth on 401, follow redirect on 3xx, etc.)
HTTP RESPONSE.Location: Must be present in 3xx redirect responses; provides the target URI for the client to follow
HTTP RESPONSE.Body: MUST NOT be present in HEAD responses; absent for 204 No Content and 304 Not Modified; present for most other success/error responses
HTTP RESPONSE.Set-Cookie: Server-side session management; client stores and re-sends as Cookie header in subsequent requests
HTTP RESPONSE.Content-Length: Required when response body is present; must match actual body byte length
HTTP RESPONSE.Connection: 'close' signals connection termination after response; 'keep-alive' (default) allows further requests on same connection

status_changes.description: State transition: INIT → TCP connect → CONNECTED → send request → RESPONSE_PENDING → receive response → IDLE (or AUTH_REQUIRED on 401, or follow redirect on 3xx, or CLOSED on Connection: close)

status_changes.description: After 301/302 redirect, the client issues a new GET request to the Location URI before proceeding with other operations
status_changes.rationale: Evidence is from LLM Spec Agent documentation referencing Session 3 trace. The session trace is indirect; also, 302 redirects may preserve the original method per RFC 7231, so the claim that GET is always issued may be an oversimplification.
